What to look for: Same person appears as officer/member/manager and registered agent.
Why it matters: Strong direct-founder signal; more likely owner-operated and reachable.
Campaign use: Use direct owner-founder messaging; validate contact before campaign.

What to look for: One person is CEO/CFO/Secretary/Director or manager and agent.
Why it matters: Very early or closely held business; likely needs setup help, website, funding readiness.
Campaign use: Good for first-wave owner support campaigns.

What to look for: Agent address matches principal or primary business address.
Why it matters: Filing likely controlled by the operator; address has stronger evidence.
Campaign use: Raises accuracy, but still verify address type before using location claims.

What to look for: Individual agent + principal at residential-style street pattern, no RA service or PO box.
Why it matters: Founder/self-filed signal; often indicates startup stage and personal-business overlap.
Campaign use: Use carefully: do not say it is a home; verify before any location-specific outreach.

What to look for: Agent is a registered corporate agent or known filing service.
Why it matters: Lower direct contact confidence; owner likely shielded by service or attorney.
Campaign use: Enrich principal/website first; do not send sales messaging to RA service by default.

What to look for: Mail-only address or commercial mail signal.
Why it matters: Lower operating-location confidence; may still be valid mailing contact.
Campaign use: Need website, phone, and physical location verification.

What to look for: Three or more principal contacts or different officers.
Why it matters: More mature than single founder; may have funding, fleet, or systems needs.

What to look for: Two or more principals share last name or address.
Why it matters: Family/closely held business; decision process may be concentrated.

What to look for: Business name or description contains rental, fleet, car, vehicle, delivery, logistics, courier, etc.
Why it matters: Direct HireCar fit for vehicle/rental/fleet services.

What to look for: CA SOS source did not provide emails, phone numbers, or websites.
Why it matters: Enrichment is required; absence is a workflow signal, not proof the company has no website.
Campaign use: Search by entity name + principal + address; record source URL and match confidence.
